## Summary
- Add `Agent / Release / Publish` for marked merged release PRs, plus manual `version`, `target_sha`, and `dry_run` recovery inputs.
- Add a typed publish CLI that validates release PR metadata, package version, changelog notes, target SHA, and tag absence before creating the GitHub Release/tag.
- Update the release prompt and versioning docs so future release PRs carry the publish marker.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`

Closes #408

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #411 closes #408 by adding a deterministic `Agent / Release / Publish` workflow after merged Sepo release PRs. It adds a typed publish CLI that validates release metadata, package version, changelog notes, target SHA, and tag absence before creating the GitHub Release/tag. The release prompt and versioning docs are updated so future release PRs carry a publish marker. The approved design goal is to publish from merged default-branch commits, not from unmerged PR heads.

## Review
The PR is directionally correct, but the manual recovery path has a privileged-runtime gap that needs a branch change before merge. Reviewers agreed the implementation is mostly focused and well tested for happy paths, but disagreed on severity: Codex marked the manual `target_sha` issue blocking, the rubric review flagged the same gap as a warning, and Claude treated the PR-triggered merged-commit path as safe.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Manual dispatch can execute unchecked target SHA | BLOCKING | `workflow_dispatch` checks out `inputs.target_sha` before resolving release-capable auth and running repo-local actions/scripts, while the CLI only shape-checks the SHA later. This can run publish code from an unmerged same-repo commit instead of trusted default-branch runtime code. |
| Release PR marker is not enforced early or deterministically | WARNING | The publish marker is prompt-injected only, so a valid release PR can silently skip publishing if the model omits it. Unmarked merged PRs also enter checkout/auth/runtime setup before the CLI skips them. |
| Safety guard branches lack regression coverage | WARNING | Tests cover dry-run, unmarked skip, manual publish, and version mismatch, but not several core guard branches such as tag-exists, target-SHA mismatch, missing required files, missing changelog notes, and prerelease flagging. |

## Progress
- Verified the live PR state, linked issue #408, PR diff, existing inline comments, and review threads.
- Existing inline comments and review threads were empty before mutation.
- Posted one inline comment on `.github/workflows/agent-release-publish.yml:49` for the unchecked manual `target_sha` checkout.
- No comments were minimized, replied to, or threads resolved.
- The PR-triggered merged-PR path does validate merged state, marker, required files, version/changelog, tag absence, and merge-commit target matching.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Manual dispatch can execute unchecked target SHA</summary>

**Cause:** `.github/workflows/agent-release-publish.yml` uses `inputs.target_sha` as the checkout ref for manual runs, then runs local actions and `.agent/dist/cli/publish-release.js` with `contents: write`. `.agent/src/release-publish.ts` only verifies that `targetSha` is a full 40-character SHA and manual runs do not prove default-branch reachability.

**Candidate solutions:** Keep the workflow checkout/runtime on the trusted default branch and treat `target_sha` only as data for release targeting, or perform a trusted default-branch reachability check before any checkout of `target_sha`. Add focused coverage for rejecting or safely handling non-default-branch target SHAs.

**Comments:** This is the only issue that should block merge. It directly conflicts with the intended invariant from #408 that release tags point at merged default-branch commits.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Release PR marker is not enforced early or deterministically</summary>

**Cause:** `.github/prompts/agent-release.md` tells the agent to include `<!-- sepo-agent-release-pr -->`, and `validateReleasePr` skips when it is missing, but no deterministic PR-creation code injects or validates the marker. The workflow job condition also allows all merged default-branch PRs to reach checkout/auth/runtime setup.

**Candidate solutions:** Deterministically inject or validate the marker when creating release PRs, or derive release intent from existing release-prepare metadata. Add a PR-event job guard such as marker detection to skip unmarked merges earlier.

**Comments:** This is fail-safe because it skips instead of mispublishing, so it is not blocking.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Safety guard branches lack regression coverage</summary>

**Cause:** The added tests do not cover several branches that enforce release safety invariants.

**Candidate solutions:** Add focused tests for duplicate tag detection, target SHA mismatch, unmerged PR rejection, missing required release files, missing changelog section, and prerelease flag creation.

**Comments:** Claude manually verified some of these branches, but regression coverage should protect them long term.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: The manual dispatch runtime issue is concrete, branch-changeable, and safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Change manual publish dispatch so release-capable steps run trusted default-branch runtime code, or verify `target_sha` is default-branch reachable before it can become the checkout ref.
- [ ] Add focused regression coverage for the manual `target_sha` trust boundary.

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #411 closes [#408](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/408) by adding a deterministic Sepo release publish path after marked release PRs merge to the default branch. It adds `Agent / Release / Publish`, a typed publish CLI, tests, release prompt marker guidance, and versioning docs. The core safety goal from #408 is that release tags point at merged default-branch commits, not unmerged PR heads. The current head is `48e1a1a2a35d28c621fa2bc3797627a4ff7c7ea4`.

## Review
The prior blocking manual `target_sha` trust-boundary issue is resolved in the current PR state. Reviewers agree the release-capable runtime now stays on trusted checkout code; remaining differences are severity only, with Claude rating two follow-ups as WARNING while Codex and the rubric review treat them as INFO/no required work.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Release PR marker depends on prompt compliance | INFO | Release PR recognition depends on the hidden marker requested in the release prompt. Omission fails closed and manual recovery exists, so this is a hardening note rather than required work. |
| Remaining guard branches could use broader tests | INFO | Current tests cover the main publish paths and the manual `target_sha` trust boundary. Extra coverage for duplicate tags, missing changelog notes, PR mismatch, and prerelease flagging would reduce future regression risk. |

## Progress
- The current workflow no longer checks out `inputs.target_sha`; manual dispatch checks out the default branch and passes `TARGET_SHA` only as data.
- The publish CLI now validates target reachability with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` before target file reads or GitHub release calls.
- Review artifacts report focused regression coverage for rejecting unmerged manual target SHAs with zero `gh` calls.
- Resolved the stale same-agent inline review thread `PRRT_kwDOSOhEMM6HLMeK`; no new inline comments, replies, or minimizations were added.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Release PR marker depends on prompt compliance</summary>

**Cause:** The marker is requested in [`.github/prompts/agent-release.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/48e1a1a2a35d28c621fa2bc3797627a4ff7c7ea4/.github/prompts/agent-release.md), and the publish CLI skips unmarked PRs.

**Candidate solutions:** Future hardening could inject release intent deterministically at PR creation time, or derive it from release-prepare metadata plus required file changes.

**Comments:** Claude marked this WARNING; Codex and the rubric review treated it as non-blocking because omission skips publishing rather than mispublishing.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Remaining guard branches could use broader tests</summary>

**Cause:** [`.agent/src/__tests__/publish-release-cli.test.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/48e1a1a2a35d28c621fa2bc3797627a4ff7c7ea4/.agent/src/__tests__/publish-release-cli.test.ts) covers the core paths but not every defensive branch in [`.agent/src/release-publish.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/48e1a1a2a35d28c621fa2bc3797627a4ff7c7ea4/.agent/src/release-publish.ts).

**Candidate solutions:** Add follow-up tests for existing tags, missing required files, missing changelog sections, PR merge-target mismatch, and prerelease releases.

**Comments:** This is useful test-depth work, but not required for the current fix because the highest-risk trust boundary is now covered.

</details>

`NO_AUTOMATED_ACTION`: No unresolved required branch-change work remains; the remaining items are optional hardening notes.
